key_insight: ImLoc shows that augmenting 2D image-based representations with per-image depth estimates recovers much of the geometric reasoning of 3D models while keeping the simplicity and updateability of image collections.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between easy-to-maintain 2D image-based localization (low geometry) and accurate but heavyweight 3D structure-based localization (costly reconstruction and updates).
method: Represent each database image as RGB + estimated depth map to encode local geometry without building a global 3D model.
Use dense image-to-image matching and geometric verification leveraging the estimated depth to compute camera poses robustly.
Keep the pipeline image-centric so databases are simple to update and maintain while preserving high localization accuracy.
impact: Offers practitioners a practical trade-off: near-3D geometric accuracy with the low-maintenance workflow of image-based systems—useful for scalable AR, robotics, and mapping deployments.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input image → depth estimator → RGBD database → dense matching → pose estimation
Before/after comparison: pure 2D retrieval vs ImLoc (with depth) showing improved pose alignment
Bar chart: accuracy vs maintenance cost for 2D, ImLoc, and 3D methods
Icon set: camera, depth map, database/update arrow to emphasize easy updates and geometry
paper_title: ImLoc: Revisiting Visual Localization with Image-based Representation
paper_authors: Xudong Jiang, Fangjinhua Wang, Silvano Galliani, Christoph Vogel, Marc Pollefeys
